examples.solution_text:
(a) Replace $y$ in the first equation using the second.
$\begin{align*}-2x+15&=3x+8\\7&=5x\\x&=\frac{7}{5}\end{align*}$
Substitute into $y=3x+8$.
$\begin{align*}y&=3\left(\frac{7}{5}\right)+8\\&=\frac{61}{5}\end{align*}$
$(x,y)=\left(\frac{7}{5},\frac{61}{5}\right)$
(b) From $x+y=17$, $y=17-x$.
$\begin{align*}0.4x+0.3(17-x)&=6.2\\0.4x+5.1-0.3x&=6.2\\0.1x&=1.1\\x&=11\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}y&=17-11\\&=6\end{align*}$
$(x,y)=(11,6)$

examples.question_text:
(a) Solve by elimination: $4x+3y=19$ and $2x-3y=11$.
(b) A student adds $7u+4v=22$ and $3u+4v=-2$. Explain why this does not remove a pronumeral, then solve the equations.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The $y$ coefficients have equal size and opposite signs, so add.
$\begin{align*}4x+3y&=19\quad(1)\\2x-3y&=11\quad(2)\end{align*}$
$(1)+(2)$:
$\begin{align*}6x&=30\\x&=5\end{align*}$
Substitute into $(1)$.
$\begin{align*}4(5)+3y&=19\\3y&=-1\\y&=-\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$
$(x,y)=\left(5,-\frac{1}{3}\right)$
(b) Adding gives $10u+8v=20$, which still has both pronumerals. Both equations have $+4v$, so subtract.
$\begin{align*}7u+4v&=22\quad(1)\\3u+4v&=-2\quad(2)\end{align*}$
$(1)-(2)$:
$\begin{align*}4u&=24\\u&=6\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}7(6)+4v&=22\\4v&=-20\\v&=-5\end{align*}$
$(u,v)=(6,-5)$

$\begin{align*}4x+3y&=53\quad(1)\\2x-y&=9\quad(2)\end{align*}$
Multiply every term of $(2)$ by $3$.
$6x-3y=27\quad(3)$
The $y$ coefficients have opposite signs, so add.
$(1)+(3)$:
$\begin{align*}10x&=80\\x&=8\end{align*}$
Substitute into $(2)$.
$\begin{align*}2(8)-y&=9\\y&=7\end{align*}$
$(x,y)=(8,7)$

$\begin{align*}2x+3y&=-1\quad(1)\\5x+4y&=29\quad(2)\end{align*}$
Multiply $(1)$ by $4$ and $(2)$ by $3$ to match the $y$ coefficients.
$\begin{align*}8x+12y&=-4\quad(3)\\15x+12y&=87\quad(4)\end{align*}$
Both have $+12y$, so subtract.
$(4)-(3)$:
$\begin{align*}7x&=91\\x&=13\end{align*}$
Substitute into $(1)$.
$\begin{align*}2(13)+3y&=-1\\3y&=-27\\y&=-9\end{align*}$
$(x,y)=(13,-9)$

examples.derivation: (a) Equating the expressions for y gives 5x=7, so x=7/5 and y=3(7/5)+8=61/5. (b) Rearranging gives y=17-x; substitution gives 0.1x=1.1, so x=11 and y=6. These follow the supplied direct and rearrangement substitution methods; decimal coefficients are a value variant.

(a) Adding eliminates y: 6x=30, hence x=5; 20+3y=19 gives y=-1/3. (b) Adding gives 10u+8v=20 and eliminates neither pronumeral. Subtracting gives 4u=24, hence u=6; 42+4v=22 gives v=-5. The explanation and methods match the supplied elimination and error-analysis activities.
Multiplying the second equation by 3 gives 6x-3y=27. Adding to the first gives 10x=80, hence x=8. Substitution into 2x-y=9 gives y=7. This matches the supplied one-equation scaling method.
Multiplying the equations by 4 and 3 gives 8x+12y=-4 and 15x+12y=87. Subtracting gives 7x=91, hence x=13. Substitution gives 26+3y=-1, so y=-9. This matches the supplied two-equation scaling method.
